name.description: Option name. Returned as `choice` and used as the key in `probabilities`. Sent to the model.
name.title: Name

description.description: What this option covers, sent on the option's line after the name. One line saying what separates it from similar options works best. Omit when the name is clear on its own.
description.title: Description

ChoiceQuestion.description: Which of these options? For a fixed set of unordered options.

id.description: Your key for this question; the answer comes back under it. Not sent to the model.
id.title: Id

instructions.description: What the model should decide, written as a complete question.
instructions.title: Instructions

options.description: The answer options (2 to 255). The model was trained on up to 16; more are read with untrained labels. Add an `other` option when the list might not cover every input.
options.title: Options

ChoiceQuestion.title: ChoiceQuestion

NoulQuestion.description: Is this true? For a clean yes/no where the probability itself is the signal.

id.description: Your key for this question; the answer comes back under it. Not sent to the model.
id.title: Id

instructions.description: The yes/no question, phrased so that yes is the outcome you want the probability of, e.g. `Does the image show food or cooking?`
instructions.title: Instructions

criteria.description: Optional. Pins down a subtle yes/no boundary.

NoulQuestion.title: NoulQuestion

ScoreQuestion.description: Which level? For a position on a spectrum you can describe.

id.description: Your key for this question; the answer comes back under it. Not sent to the model.
id.title: Id

instructions.description: What the model should rate, written as a complete question.
instructions.title: Instructions

levels.description: Ordered level descriptions, low end to high end (2 to 10). A level's number is its index, starting at 0. Six levels use the model's native 0-5 score; any other number is read as a choice over the levels.
levels.title: Levels

ScoreQuestion.title: ScoreQuestion

state.description: The text to evaluate: a string, or a JSON object / array of related context (messages, records, a policy). Every question sees the same state and images. May be empty when `images` carries the content. Input over the model's token limit is rejected, never truncated.
examples: Seller title: wireless earbuds, barely used
state.title: State

images.description: Up to 8 images the questions are about, placed before the state. Large images cost more tokens and time; about 448 px on the long side is enough for most decisions.
images.title: Images

choices.description: Choice questions: pick one option from a set.
choices.title: Choices

scores.description: Score questions: place the state on ordered levels.
scores.title: Scores

nouls.description: Noul questions: probability that the answer is yes.
nouls.title: Nouls
